title: Truth Tables and Combined Logic

code_first.q: Trace combined Boolean logic in an illustrative network-security alert.
code_first.code:
// A: unknown device; B: repeated failures; C: reported malware
A = true
B = false
C = true
if (A AND B) OR C then
    print("Investigate")
endif
p: Predict the output for A=true, B=false and C=true.
Change C to false and predict.
Describe one security event represented by A, B or C, and explain why this is only a simplified alert rule.
code_first.a: With A AND B=false but C=true, the full expression is true, so Investigate prints. Setting C=false produces no output. A represents an unknown device, B repeated failures and C a reported malware incident. Real security alerts need evidence and more sophisticated rules; this code does not identify malware.

original_exam_questions: How many rows are needed for a 3-input truth table? [2 marks]
Evaluate (A AND B) OR C when A=1 B=0 C=1. [2 marks]
Explain the benefit of an intermediate X column. [2 marks]
Allows accurate separate evaluation of one gate and helps trace errors in combined expressions.

optional_original_challenge.coreHint: (A AND B) OR C is true whenever C is true.

stretch.task: Change C to false and test both values of B.
stretch.hint: Compute intermediate A AND B first.
stretch.answer: With A=true, B=false, C=false there is no output. With B=true, it prints Investigate.

mastery.task: Write a small program or full truth table for (A AND B) OR C. Compare a case where C overrides the AND condition.
mastery.hint: Eight input rows and an intermediate X column.
